Hi, I had all kinds of rigs, from one with tripple SLI GTX470 (extreme loud) to water cooled Titan (extreme silent(but expensive)). So my next idea is to build an air cooled case which is silent no matter what parts you use. Following paint masterpiece shows my idea: Concept drawing

The long explanation: You might recognized when you close a (car)window that it instantly get's quiet as soon as the last bit is closed. So we can assume that a complete closed box is very silent. But our parts need air so we somehow have to get air inside without letting sound outside. Now imagine a tube which is filled with soundproof material except a hole in the middle. If you scream in this tube it's nearly impossible to hear you on the other side. So we assume that if you let air flow trough a well isolated path (with edges) it should be silent. Combined we get a case in a case with two slots where air can get in and out. Also a well isolated part where you can get all the cables trough.

So is here a sound engineer or someone with experience who can validate this idea?
Is an air cooled sound proof case possible? Idea and concept in description.

How quiet you get your PC is really going to depend on what you want to do with it. Check out SPCR if you haven't before.

Silent computing is a thing and it's a delicate balance between noise and cooling. I think the issue with your idea is that air flow is severely restricted so you'll have a hard time keeping components cool.

A better alternative is to go with a good air flow case and use all fanless components; think SSD, fanless case, fanless PSU, fanless heatsinks. No mechanical parts means no noise. Obviously, you're going to have issues with heavy duty processing and gaming but it's complete fine for browsing and watching movies.

More practical, which is what I have, is to get components that run cool, that spin up fans on load, and a good air flow case. It's almost silent normally because fans noise don't raise above ambient noise. Fans will spin up during gaming but my headphones block it out. Even then fan don't need to run full speed. For example, my overclocked GTX970 only spin up fans to 50% - 60% on load and no fans at all during idle.

You would do better with isolation mounts for your fans, sound absorbing foam inside and very large, low RPM fans. With graphics cards you get what you get but EVGA's ACX2 system is very quiet in my rig. CPU and PSU fans will probably need to be replaced with <25dB models and mounted with isolating rubber bushings. I think some prudent purchases could build a very quiet gaming rig.

The problems with your design are sound proofing (sound will pass through the air tunnel both perpendicular and along the air channel) and resistance. High resistance means a bigger load which means a faster fan which means a louder fan. Unrestricted airflow is itself more quiet and requires less energy to maintain bringing down the overall noise level.

Sport hunting, when done right is very beneficial to the local population and the economy. That money typically goes towards conservative efforts for those animals. In Africa, they don't care about preservation of species, the people want either money or food. Hunters provide both the money and donate the meat to local villages.

Sometimes the rare/endangered animals being hunted are negatively impacting their environment. Sterile older males killing young cubs is a great example.
